title: Domestication of cattle, sheep and goats
summary: Sheep and goats came under domestication, probably independently of one another and possibly several times, in the region from the northern Zagros to southeastern Anatolia between about 11,000 and 10,500 years ago. Taurine cattle were first domesticated somewhere in the upper Euphrates Valley between about 11,000 and 10,000 years ago. These animals later spread through the Mediterranean Basin.

uncertainty.note: Zeder (2008) dates initial goat and cattle domestication to ca. 11,000–10,000 BP (c. 9050–8050 BCE), with morphologically domestic cattle and pigs reaching wider regions by 8500–8000 BP (c. 6550–6050 BCE); World History Encyclopedia records managed wild sheep by 9000 BCE and domestic cattle by 6000 BCE.

importance.justification: The domestication of cattle, sheep, and goats provided the primary animal protein, dairy, fertilizer, and traction foundation for Old World agricultural civilizations across several continents for millennia.

related.because: The package of domestic sheep, goats, and cattle was carried by migrating Neolithic farming communities westward across the Mediterranean basin and Europe.
